ddx.vs: B-prolymphocytes are typically round-nucleated with a prominent central nucleolus and express B-cell markers rather than CD3/CD7 with TCL1 overexpression.
ATLL shows polylobated 'flower cells' with more condensed chromatin and is HTLV-1 positive and usually CD7 negative, CD25 positive.
Hairy cells have pale gray-blue cytoplasm with circumferential hairy projections and oval/bean-shaped nuclei rather than deeply basophilic cytoplasm.

61935.recognize_zh: 中央嗜中性球核分葉、染色質粗，細胞質右緣有一塊淡藍色區域（Döhle body／細胞質嗜鹼性），加上細胞質內散在的紫色顆粒，提示毒性變化（toxic changes）。
features: Mature neutrophil about 1.5 times red cell diameter with a lobulated, coarsely clumped nucleus
Pale cytoplasm with scattered fine-to-coarse purple granules
Ill-defined pale blue cytoplasmic patch at the right edge of the cell, consistent with a Döhle body/toxic cytoplasmic basophilia
No obvious cytoplasmic vacuoles
Background red cells include several crenated forms (echinocytes, likely artifactual) and scattered platelets
61935.describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows normocytic red cells with some crenated forms, likely drying artifact, and scattered platelets. The central neutrophil has a lobated nucleus with coarse chromatin and cytoplasm containing scattered purple granules. A pale blue, poorly demarcated area is present at the right periphery of the cytoplasm, representing a Döhle body or focal toxic basophilia. Vacuolization is not evident. Findings are consistent with a neutrophil showing toxic changes, typically reactive to infection, inflammation, burns or cytokine therapy.

ddx.vs: MYH9 inclusions are larger, more sharply defined and angular, present in most granulocytes, and accompanied by giant platelets and thrombocytopenia.
Normal neutrophils lack blue cytoplasmic patches and have only fine, inconspicuous lilac granules.
A band has a continuous non-segmented C- or S-shaped nucleus; toxic change is judged independently from nuclear shape.

60399.recognize_zh: 畫面中央最大的細胞呈圓形、核質比中等，核染色質細緻散開並可見淡色核仁，細胞質藍染且散布紫紅色嗜天青顆粒（azurophilic granules），周圍有較成熟的髓細胞與帶狀核細胞可作比較，符合前髓細胞（promyelocyte）。
features: Large cell, clearly larger than surrounding myelocytes and metamyelocytes
Round to oval nucleus with finely dispersed chromatin and a faint nucleolus
Moderate N:C ratio with a rim of basophilic cytoplasm
Fine purple-red primary (azurophilic) granules overlying cytoplasm and nucleus
Background of maturing granulocytes (myelocytes, metamyelocytes, bands) typical of marrow aspirate
60399.describe_en: Bone marrow aspirate smear shows maturing granulocytic elements, including myelocytes, metamyelocytes and band forms. The central cell is large, with a round nucleus, finely dispersed chromatin, a visible nucleolus and basophilic cytoplasm containing scattered azurophilic granules that overlie the nucleus. No Auer rods or bundled granules are seen. Findings are consistent with a normal promyelocyte.

ddx.vs: Myeloblasts are smaller with a higher N:C ratio and scant or no azurophilic granules, whereas this cell has abundant primary granules.
Myelocytes have more condensed chromatin, no nucleolus and pinkish cytoplasm with specific granules and a distinct Golgi zone, unlike the granular basophilic cytoplasm and fine chromatin here.
APL promyelocytes show bilobed or folded nuclei, coarse dense granules or Auer rod bundles (faggot cells), which are absent in this cell.
Proerythroblasts have deep blue agranular cytoplasm and coarser chromatin, lacking the azurophilic granules seen here.

111.recognize_zh: 骨髓抹片可見核分離、雙核圓形的小型發育不良巨核細胞（separated-nuclei megakaryocytes）與成群的巨母細胞樣紅血球前驅細胞，末梢血白血球稀少且有大紅血球；核型與 FISH 都只剩一條第 7 號染色體（monosomy 7），配合兒童年齡與低芽細胞比例，指向兒童難治性血球低下（RCC）。
features: Dysplastic megakaryocytes with two or more widely separated, round nuclei (aspirate) and small hypolobated forms (biopsy)
Clusters of immature erythroid precursors with megaloblastoid, finely stippled open chromatin and deeply basophilic cytoplasm; occasional irregular or budding erythroid nuclei
No increase in blasts apparent on aspirate or biopsy fields
Peripheral blood: sparse leukocytes (lymphocytes, monocyte, a mature neutrophil) with mild anisocytosis and occasional macrocytes
Biopsy low power: cellular trilineage marrow in the field shown; scattered hemosiderin pigment
Karyotype 45,XY,-7 (single chromosome 7, arrow) and interphase FISH with one CEP7 (green) and one 7q31 (red) signal
111.describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows leukopenia with few circulating leukocytes, mild anisocytosis with occasional macrocytes, and no circulating blasts identified. The bone marrow aspirate shows dysplastic megakaryocytes with widely separated round nuclei and clusters of erythroid precursors with megaloblastoid chromatin and occasional nuclear irregularity; blasts are not increased. The core biopsy shows trilineage hematopoiesis with small hypolobated megakaryocytes and immature erythroid islands; the low-power field illustrated appears cellular rather than hypocellular, so overall cellularity should be judged on the entire core against age-matched norms. Conventional cytogenetics shows 45,XY,-7 and interphase FISH confirms loss of one chromosome 7 (one CEP7 and one D7S486 signal). Findings are consistent with refractory cytopenia of childhood (childhood MDS with low blasts) with monosomy 7.

ddx.vs: Aplastic anemia lacks megakaryocytic dysplasia and clustered immature erythroid islands and does not carry monosomy 7, which is disease-defining evidence of a clonal myeloid neoplasm.

Megaloblastic change affects all lineages with giant metamyelocytes and hypersegmented neutrophils, reverses with vitamin replacement, and has no clonal cytogenetic abnormality; vitamin levels were normal here.

ddx.dx: Inherited bone marrow failure (e.g., Fanconi anemia, SAMD9/SAMD9L or GATA2 syndromes)
ddx.vs: Morphology overlaps, so germline testing, chromosome breakage studies and family history are needed; these syndromes can themselves evolve to monosomy 7 MDS.

ddx.dx: MDS with increased blasts / juvenile myelomonocytic leukemia
ddx.vs: Blasts are below 2% in blood and 5% in marrow here, and there is no monocytosis, leukocytosis or splenomegaly as expected in JMML.

captions: Bone marrow core biopsy, low power: cellular trilineage marrow in this field (H&E)
Peripheral blood, low power: sparse leukocytes with mild anisocytosis
Peripheral blood, high power: mature segmented neutrophil and occasional macrocytes
Core biopsy, high power: megakaryocytes with separated nuclei and immature erythroid cells
Core biopsy, high power: erythroid cluster, small megakaryocytes and hemosiderin
Core biopsy, high power: clusters of immature erythroid precursors
Aspirate: dysplastic megakaryocyte with widely separated round nuclei beside pronormoblasts
Aspirate: megaloblastoid erythroid precursors with open stippled chromatin
Aspirate: megaloblastoid erythroid precursors, one with irregular budding nucleus, and a pigment-laden cell
Karyotype 45,XY,-7 with loss of one chromosome 7 (arrow)
Interphase FISH: one CEP7 (green) and one 7q31 (red) signal, indicating monosomy 7

47.recognize_zh: 骨髓切片中有界線不清的淋巴組織球性浸潤，以小淋巴球和組織球為主，只散在少數核大、染色質淡的大型異型細胞；膜型 B 細胞標記只標出這些散在的大細胞，背景小細胞多被 T 細胞標記染色，符合 T 細胞/組織球豐富型大 B 細胞淋巴瘤（THRLBCL）侵犯骨髓。
features: Scattered single large atypical cells with vesicular, irregular to oval nuclei and small nucleoli, not forming sheets or clusters
Large cells show membranous positivity for an (unlabeled) B-cell marker and nuclear positivity for a second unlabeled marker, while the background small cells are negative
Predominant background of small, slightly irregular lymphocytes that stain for a membranous T-cell-type marker, admixed with numerous histiocytes with pale to eosinophilic cytoplasm
Ill-defined, poorly circumscribed interstitial/paratrabecular lymphohistiocytic infiltrate replacing hematopoietic marrow at low power
Residual fat spaces and bony trabeculae; no discrete B-cell nodules or follicular dendritic meshworks evident
47.describe_en: Bone marrow core biopsy shows an ill-defined lymphohistiocytic infiltrate occupying intertrabecular spaces and replacing normal hematopoiesis. At high power the infiltrate is composed predominantly of small, slightly irregular lymphocytes and numerous histiocytes, among which scattered single large atypical cells with vesicular nuclei and small nucleoli are present. Immunohistochemistry (markers not labeled in the images) shows membranous staining of the scattered large cells for a B-cell-type marker and nuclear staining of the large cells for a second marker, whereas the background small lymphocytes are diffusely positive for a membranous T-cell-type marker. No sheets of large cells or discrete small B-cell nodules are seen. In the clinical context of splenomegaly and pancytopenia, findings are consistent with marrow involvement by T-cell/histiocyte-rich large B-cell lymphoma; the TCR gene rearrangement result likely reflects the reactive T-cell background rather than a T-cell lymphoma.

ddx.vs: Hodgkin/Reed-Sternberg cells are CD30+/CD15+ with weak PAX5 and absent CD20/OCT2/BOB1, and marrow involvement usually shows fibrosis, whereas the large cells here are strongly CD20-type positive.

ddx.dx: Nodular lymphocyte-predominant Hodgkin lymphoma (T-cell-rich variant pattern)
ddx.vs: NLPHL retains at least focal small B-cell nodules with CD21+ FDC meshworks and PD-1+ T-cell rosettes around LP cells, while THRLBCL lacks residual small B-cell nodules in a diffuse T-cell/histiocyte background.

ddx.dx: Peripheral T-cell lymphoma, NOS or angioimmunoblastic T-cell lymphoma
ddx.vs: The atypical large cells in PTCL/AITL are T cells (often with antigen loss or TFH markers), with scattered B immunoblasts being small and EBV-associated, whereas here the atypical large cells are B cells and the small T cells lack cytologic atypia.

ddx.dx: Reactive lymphohistiocytic aggregate or granulomatous marrow lesion
ddx.vs: Reactive aggregates lack atypical large B cells, which are the diagnostic population highlighted by the B-cell marker in this case.

captions: IHC, membranous B-cell-type marker highlighting scattered single large cells in a negative small-cell background
H&E, low power: marrow core with ill-defined interstitial lymphohistiocytic infiltrate between trabeculae
H&E, medium power: infiltrate of small lymphocytes and histiocytes replacing hematopoiesis
H&E, high power: small irregular lymphocytes and pale histiocytes with scattered large vesicular atypical cells
IHC, nuclear marker (unlabeled) strongly positive in scattered large cells, weak to negative in small cells
IHC, high power: membranous T-cell-type marker staining the majority of small lymphocytes, sparing histiocytes
IHC, low power: membranous marker diffusely highlighting the small lymphocytes of the infiltrate
IHC, low power: nuclear marker (unlabeled) staining numerous scattered small cells throughout the marrow

65199.recognize_zh: 末梢血可見中性球增多並有左移、嗜鹼性球，箭頭標示核固縮的壞死性中性球（necrobiotic neutrophils）；骨髓極度增生、骨髓系與紅血球系比例升高，巨核細胞增多且多為小型、單葉、成群聚集（CD61 凸顯），這些是 CML 慢性期的典型骨髓樣貌，只是發生在 3 歲幼童。
features: PB (A): leukocytosis with neutrophilia, left shift and basophils; arrows mark necrobiotic neutrophils with pyknotic condensed nuclei
Aspirate (B): myeloid left shift with increased myeloid:erythroid ratio, no increase in blasts; occasional necrobiotic neutrophils (arrows)
Aspirate (C): cluster of megakaryocytes, many small with hypolobated/unilobated nuclei
Biopsy H&E (D): hypercellular marrow (>90%) with granulocytic hyperplasia and increased small megakaryocytes
CD61 (E): numerous small, clustered megakaryocytes throughout the core
65199.describe_en: The peripheral blood smear shows neutrophilic leukocytosis with left shift, basophils and scattered necrobiotic neutrophils with pyknotic nuclei; platelets appear increased. The bone marrow aspirate shows marked granulocytic hyperplasia with a high myeloid-to-erythroid ratio and no increase in blasts, along with clusters of small, hypolobated megakaryocytes. The core biopsy is hypercellular (>90%) with granulocytic proliferation and increased small megakaryocytes, highlighted by CD61. In conjunction with t(9;22)(q34;q11.2) and a BCR::ABL1 p210 (e14a2) fusion, the findings are consistent with chronic myeloid leukemia, chronic phase, in a young child.

ddx.vs: ET has large to giant hyperlobulated megakaryocytes without marked granulocytic left shift or basophilia, whereas CML shows small hypolobated 'dwarf' megakaryocytes and requires exclusion by BCR::ABL1 testing.
Reactive neutrophilia has toxic changes and lacks basophilia, small clustered megakaryocytes and the Philadelphia chromosome.
JMML in young children shows monocytosis, circulating erythroid precursors, elevated HbF and RAS-pathway mutations rather than basophilia and BCR::ABL1.
aCML has prominent dysgranulopoiesis without basophilia, and CNL shows mature neutrophilia with CSF3R mutation; both are BCR::ABL1-negative.

64175.recognize_zh: 周邊血液中三顆小型淋巴樣細胞，圓核、染色質呈塊狀，胞質比一般淋巴球略多且帶藍色，外觀介於淋巴球與漿細胞之間（plasmacytoid lymphocytes）；背景紅血球有疊錢狀排列（rouleaux），提示血中有 IgM 單株蛋白。
features: Three small to intermediate lymphoid cells with round, slightly eccentric nuclei
Moderately clumped chromatin without conspicuous nucleoli
Modest amount of basophilic cytoplasm, more than a typical small lymphocyte (plasmacytoid features)
No perinuclear hof or distinct plasma cell clock-face chromatin
Background red cells arranged in short rouleaux stacks
Few platelets, no smudge cells in this field
64175.describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows several small to intermediate lymphoid cells with round, slightly eccentric nuclei, clumped chromatin, and a moderate rim of basophilic cytoplasm, imparting a plasmacytoid appearance intermediate between lymphocytes and plasma cells. The red cells show rouleaux formation. No blasts, smudge cells, or prominent nucleoli are seen. Findings are suggestive of circulating lymphoplasmacytic cells with a paraproteinemia, consistent with Waldenstrom macroglobulinemia in the appropriate clinical setting (IgM paraprotein, MYD88 L265P).

ddx.vs: CLL cells have scant cytoplasm with soccer-ball chromatin and smudge cells and are CD5+/CD23+, without plasmacytoid features or IgM rouleaux.

ddx.dx: Plasma cell myeloma / plasma cell leukemia
ddx.vs: Plasma cells have eccentric nuclei with a perinuclear hof and more abundant cytoplasm, and are CD138+/CD19- without a B-cell component.

ddx.dx: Marginal zone lymphoma with plasmacytic differentiation
ddx.vs: Splenic MZL cells often have villous cytoplasmic projections and usually lack MYD88 L265P, which is present in over 90% of WM.
Reactive forms are heterogeneous with a spectrum of sizes and are polyclonal without a monoclonal IgM spike.

3503.recognize_zh: 骨髓抹片中一顆組織球（右側腎形核）的胞質內吞入了一顆有分葉核的細胞（位於清亮空泡中），胞質上方另有粗大黑褐色顆粒，符合噬血現象（hemophagocytosis）；形態本身無法分辨家族性或續發性 HLH。
features: Macrophage with abundant pale blue, vacuolated cytoplasm and an eccentric kidney-shaped nucleus
Engulfed nucleated cell with a lobulated dark nucleus lying within a clear phagocytic vacuole
Coarse dark brown-black granular pigment/debris in the cytoplasmic process (likely hemosiderin or ingested material)
Dendritic cytoplasmic extensions among surrounding red cells
Background red cells with refractile drying artifact inclusions
3503.describe_en: Bone marrow aspirate smear shows a macrophage with abundant pale vacuolated cytoplasm and an eccentric kidney-shaped nucleus, containing an engulfed nucleated cell with a lobulated nucleus (likely a granulocyte) within a phagocytic vacuole. Coarse dark pigmented granules are also present in the cytoplasm. The surrounding red cells show drying artifact. Findings demonstrate hemophagocytosis, consistent with hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis in the appropriate clinical and laboratory setting; hemophagocytosis alone is neither sensitive nor specific, and familial HLH requires genetic testing (e.g., PRF1, UNC13D, STX11, STXBP2).

ddx.dx: Secondary (acquired) HLH due to infection, malignancy, or autoimmunity (macrophage activation syndrome)
ddx.vs: Morphology is identical; distinction relies on age, family history, genetic testing, and identification of triggers such as EBV or lymphoma.

ddx.dx: Non-specific hemophagocytosis after transfusion or infection
ddx.vs: Isolated hemophagocytosis can occur without HLH, so diagnosis requires HLH-2004 criteria such as fever, cytopenias, ferritin, triglycerides, and soluble CD25.
True phagocytosis shows the ingested cell within a clear vacuole enclosed by macrophage cytoplasm, rather than a cell merely lying on top.

60143.recognize_zh: 骨髓抹片中多數為中到大型胚細胞，核大、部分呈腎形或摺疊、染色質細緻，細胞質中等量呈灰藍色並帶細小空泡或顆粒；旁邊有數顆染色質呈塊狀的紅血球前驅細胞可作對照。形態上難分譜系，需流式細胞儀確認混合表型急性白血病。
features: Predominance of intermediate to large blasts with high to moderate N:C ratio
Nuclei round, oval, reniform or folded, with finely dispersed chromatin and faint nucleoli
Moderate grey-blue cytoplasm, some with fine vacuoles or sparse fine granules; no Auer rods seen
Admixed erythroid precursors (small round nuclei with coarse clumped chromatin) serve as size reference
Heterogeneous blast size, with a smaller blast with scant cytoplasm near the center
60143.describe_en: Bone marrow aspirate smear shows a predominance of intermediate to large blasts with round to reniform or folded nuclei, finely dispersed chromatin, faint nucleoli, and moderate amounts of grey-blue cytoplasm containing occasional fine vacuoles; no Auer rods are identified. A smaller blast with scant cytoplasm is also present, and scattered erythroid precursors with coarse chromatin are admixed. The blast population is heterogeneous in size. Findings are consistent with acute leukemia with increased blasts; lineage assignment requires flow cytometry, and with co-expression of B-lymphoid and myeloid/monocytic markers and KMT2A rearrangement the findings support mixed phenotype acute leukemia.

ddx.vs: Morphologically similar blasts and promonocytes are separated from MPAL only by the absence of B- or T-lineage–defining antigens on flow cytometry.
B-ALL blasts are typically smaller and more uniform with scant cytoplasm and lack MPO or monocytic marker expression.

ddx.dx: Acute leukemia with bilineal (two separate) populations mimicking MPAL
ddx.vs: Flow cytometry distinguishes two discrete blast populations (bilineal) from a single population co-expressing both lineages (biphenotypic), both of which qualify as MPAL but must exclude therapy-related or defining genetic AML.
